I000.function: Fires on the first digit of the converted (feet) number right after an opening bracket following a metric length like '15 metres ('; a weaker secondary response on auxiliary/perfect verbs (was, has since, has shown) in encyclopedic sentences.

I001.function: Mixed, low-specificity detector: fires on function words and punctuation that continue a clause (of, as, a, that, comma, apostrophe) plus occasional digits; no single pattern.

I002.function: Fires inside romanized Japanese titles and names, on the mid-word fragments or particles (no, ga, naki, Taga Tame) of a transliterated phrase; also weakly on name-fragment tokens like initials.

I003.function: Fires on the day-of-month digit, the space, or the month name in a date being written out (March 31, August 2, February 1899), i.e. the point where a day or year number is about to or just did follow a month; also on 'C.' in C.S.A./C.S.S.

I004.function: Fires on later pieces of a multi-token person name, especially Japanese or Indian names (Fujii, Motoyama, Mizuki, Fernandez), and on possessive or comma right after a surname; also on a stray space before a decimal digit.

I005.function: Fires on the second year digit in season ranges like 1983-84, and on list-continuing or example-introducing tokens (comma in a list of places, 'such' before 'as', 'g' in e.g.).

I006.function: Fires on digits inside a year that is being spelled out piece by piece (18[6]9, 20[1]4, 19[8]5), especially the third digit after a month/day; also 'of' in 'June of that year'.

I007.function: Fires on the punctuation or connector that opens a parenthetical, appositive or list item in the middle of a sentence (comma, open bracket, em dash, 'the', 'and') and on the comma inside numbers like 5@,@000; expects an elaboration to follow.

I008.function: Fires on a word in a clause about stopping, reducing, forgetting or continuing despite something (still, reduced, no longer, abandoned, not, although); the context is negation or change of state of a thing, usually just before its object.

I009.function: Fires on the middle or end fragments of a multi-token proper name of South Asian or Japanese origin (Charu, Deshmukh, Sujoy Ghosh, Madhuri, Anupama); the detector is about being inside a foreign personal name.

I010.function: Fires on the first digit of a count of things (goals, accidents, licence holders, units) or on a spelled-out count word (three, four) right where a quantity is stated, such as 'scoring 48 goals' or 'there were 27 accidents'.

I011.function: Fires on tokens that state or set up a quantity of members or items: 'comprising', 'comprised', 'enough', 'many', 'number', 'some', and first digits of large counts; about the size or composition of a set.
I011.category: quantity or composition of a group

I012.function: Fires on verbs and nouns of recording, observing, firing or doing work (observations, recorded, recording, photograph, fired, flown, published, season), in a context of scientific or operational activity; mixed with a few year digits.

I013.function: Responds to digits after 'metres (' and also to words about growth, operations and commercial use in the general-aviation/fishing policy text (number, demand, operations, Increases, development, uses, commercial).

I014.function: Fires on punctuation and tokens that close a citation, title or heading fragment (comma after 'C.S.A.', closing quote, closing bracket after a year, period after a score note) and on words in section headings like 'Original design'.

I015.function: Fires on a digit inside a year (1853, 2011, 1918) right after a month-day, especially the second digit, plus a few odd tokens in scores (2-1, 7-3).

I016.function: Fires on the first digit (or space before it) of the metric conversion inside brackets after an imperial measure, e.g. '7 inches (180 mm', '300 yards (180-270', '9,110 pounds (4,'.

I017.function: Fires on the first digit of the bracketed second-unit conversion right after a length in metres or miles or inches, e.g. '17 metres (56 ft)', '20 miles (32 km)'.

I018.function: Fires on words that link a cause to a result or continue a process (leading to, resulting in, creating, win, of, greater, -ing), predicting an outcome or consequence phrase next; also a few stray date digits.

I019.function: Fires on later fragments of a person's name that follows a title or role such as critic, director or illustrator (Saibal Chatterjee, Sujoy Ghosh, Raja Sen, Mizuki Tsuge), including initials and the period after them.

I020.function: Mixed detector for ends of units in a citation or caption: punctuation closing a clause or parenthesis, 'at' before a place, and year last digits. Low coherence.

I021.function: Fires on an apostrophe or possessive 's marker after a noun or name, on ordinal suffix 'th', and on closing quotes; essentially the possessive/clitic or suffix token attached to a preceding word.

I022.function: Fires on the start or middle fragment of a person name, especially right after a first name (Varinder Aggarwal, Riteish Deshmukh, Kim Neely); also on an opening quote after 'remarked that'.

I023.function: Fires on the unit word after a number in a measurement: mph, in, inch, mm, km/h, kg, micrometres; also on the end of a compound descriptive adjective (diamond-shaped).

I024.function: Fires inside romanized Japanese phrases (Senjo no Valkyria 3: Namo naki Chikai, Moshimo Kimi ga) on the mid-word syllables and particles; a close variant of Japanese-title detector, strongest on 'o', 'no', 'ga', 'ame', 'aki'.

I025.function: Fires on prepositions and articles in a technical chemistry description of a reaction (addition of a sulfur ylide to a ketone, with, after) and on digits of a discovery year; about the grammar of reagent-substrate relations.

I026.function: Fires on tokens just before a year or date in a sentence about when something was released, opened, published or departed (released, opened, published, on, from, and 1960s), plus the space before a year; about to specify a time.

I027.function: Fires on a digit within a four-digit year (20[1]1, 19[9]8, 18[6]2, 19[2]0), mainly the third digit, and on 'of' in 'early summer of 18..'.

I028.function: Fires on tokens in measurement-heavy ship and weapon descriptions: the open bracket or space before a converted number (30.5 cm (12), 47 mm (1@.), pounds (23), kW), plus adjectives in a weapon name (quick-firing, calibre); mixed with some stray tokens.

I029.function: Fires on a mid-word token of a multi-piece or technical compound (Bill-board, enanti-oselective, En-ne-ad, Im-hot-ep, vul-can-alis, stained glass, top grossing), where a word continues across tokens.

I030.function: Fires on the open bracket or the first digit of the converted number after an imperial measure (pounds (6,000), feet (12 m), miles (32 km)), and on 'if' or 'soldiers' occasionally.

I031.function: Fires on a month name or time-span word in a date range (between February and April, May 15-18, rest of the night, one day before), and on the final digit of a season like 2011-12; about time-period boundaries.

I032.function: Fires on clause-ending or clause-joining punctuation, mainly comma, period, semicolon, closing bracket and 'and', after a place name, a list of names or a measurement in a narrative sentence.

I033.function: Fires on sentence or clause ends after a descriptive noun phrase, especially closing bracket, period after a taxonomic family or record, comma, and em dash; about the point where a definitional statement finishes.

I034.function: Fires on tokens expressing sequence or span between two things (and, to, before, precedes, for, the) in 'between X and Y', 'from X to Y', 'before doing', 'leading up to'; also a few year digits.

I035.function: Fires on sentence-ending or clause-ending punctuation (period, comma, semicolon, closing bracket) after a named place or event, and on the space after a section heading; also on the decimal separators in 1@.@8.

I036.function: Mixed. Fires on the first digit of a death year in life-span dates (1895-1973), on heading equals signs, on name fragments, and on prepositions like 'by' and 'to'. No clear single function.

I037.function: Fires on an auxiliary or copula (had, was, were, didn't, of) that comes after a subject noun phrase, expecting a verb phrase or 'to' next; also first digits in metre brackets.

I038.function: Fires on the first digit of the foot/mile conversion after a metric length in brackets, such as '17 metres (56 ft)', '20 miles (32 km)'; extremely consistent.

I039.function: Fires on verbs and adverbs of expectation, hope, worry, belief or plan (expected, hoped, hoping, felt, planned, presumably, worried, normally, hopes), where a that-clause or infinitive complement is about to follow.

I040.function: Fires on late name pieces of surnames (Fujii, Madero, Diaz, Sakimoto) and on attitude words like 'felt', 'worried', 'increasingly', 'of course'; a mix of name endings and stance words.

I041.function: Fires on middle fragments of a split foreign name or word (Betancourt, Ignazio, Pigna, Thakur, Grazia, Uggleby) and on initial-period or colon markers inside titles; about being mid-token in rare names.

I042.function: Fires on a rank, title or office word inside a multi-part title (Vice President of, Chief Coiner, Rear Admiral, Captain, Majesty, ordinal suffix nd/st before Lt.), where the next token continues the title or name.

I043.function: Fires on tokens inside official titles and unit designations (Chief, Maj., Rear Admiral, Ministry of, Committee on, 1st Battle Squadron, His Majesty), where an institution or name follows.

I044.function: Fires on the first digit (or space or open bracket) of the metric conversion after feet/inches/miles, e.g. '414 feet 2 inches (126', '20-25 mile (32'; same slot as other measure-conversion detectors, with feet and inches especially.

I045.function: Responds to digits after 'metres (' and to nouns for uses or users of airfields (development, uses, aircraft, users) in text about aviation land-use pressure.

I046.function: Fires on an auxiliary or complementizer (had, did, were, that, was, and) that follows a reporting or condition clause, expecting the verb of a embedded statement; also i.e., CAT, and possessive s.

I047.function: Fires on the open bracket or first digit of the converted number following a measurement (30.5 cm (12 in), 1,000 acres (4 km), 189 feet (57)), plus 'handful' and counts like 49.

I048.function: Fires on tokens that open a parenthetical or appositive: commas, 'the', open bracket, em dash, 'such' (as), 'well' (as), plus the comma inside numbers like 5@,@000.

I049.function: Fires on proper-name fragments and the word after a name start (Mint, Los Angeles, Boston, NHL L, motu proprio) and on varied small words (on, began, its); mostly the point where a known multi-word name completes.

I050.function: Fires on the modal-chain tokens in a conditional or hypothetical clause ('would have', 'would be', 'he would', 'would not', 'would have resulted in'), predicting a conditional consequence; also digits after 'metres ('.

I051.function: Fires on a number word or first digit giving a count in sports or military statistics (appeared in six games, scored seven points, only one goal, four of the, 174 enlisted men).

I052.function: Fires on time-unit nouns or month names and the final year digit in temporal expressions (night, December, year, month, day, engagement, 200[6], 201[0]); about the time-of-event slot.

I053.function: Mixed, low-specificity detector firing on closing quotes, 'of', 'in' after measurements, era markers (BC, s in decade), year digits, relative pronouns. No clear shared function.

I054.function: Fires on month names and the day digit in dates (February 16, August 2, October 19, February 21), and on a mix of proper-name pieces (James River, Hall, Ledger, League Island, OBE).

I055.function: Fires on words that carry an evaluative or modal expectation into a clause (expecting, existing, effect, readily to, Funding, so much, which, spend, for, annoying); mixed, loosely about a complement coming next.

I056.function: Fires on tokens before or inside a time expression: 'between 1925 and', 'in 19 years', 'down from', 'published', 'any team in', 'until publication of'; about spans of years and boundaries.

I057.function: Fires on the first digit of the metric conversion after 'metres (' and on 'would be' in a hypothetical clause ('it would be eminently', 'would be counterfeited').

I058.function: Fires on clause-ending punctuation (comma, period, semicolon, closing bracket) and on the apostrophe in possessives after a plural noun (Children's, gods' names); about the point where an item in a list, cast or aside ends.

I059.function: Fires on prepositions and articles in technical descriptions of a process: 'addition of a', 'ylide to a', 'after a burn', 'for the synthesis', 'with substituted'; about the slot right before the object or substrate of a reaction.
